issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents as int, but the solution implementation declares it as long. This attribute type mismatch is structural: students guided by the UML will implement an int field, but the provided solution/skeleton uses a long, which will cause confusion and compilation issues when combined with other int-typed attributes and methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent with the UML. Change numberOfInscribedStudents in the solution (and constructor parameter) from long to int to match the problem statement UML. Alternatively, if large counts are intended, update the UML and all method signatures/return types to use long consistently.

issues.description: The constructor in the solution uses a long parameter for numberOfInscribedStudents while the problem UML and task description specify an int in this position and order. This constructor parameter type mismatch will confuse students about the expected type and can cause compile-time type issues when implementing or comparing to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the UML: change the second constructor parameter in the solution from long to int (and assign to an int field). If a long is intentionally required, update the UML and task description to specify long and adjust return types where necessary.

issues.description: The UML and task specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int. The solution implements this method returning int, but its implementation adds numberOfInscribedStudents (declared as long in the solution) to an int, producing a long expression that cannot be returned as int without narrowing. This combination of attribute and method types creates a compile-time inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure consistent numeric types across attributes and methods. Preferred fix: change numberOfInscribedStudents to int so getTotalNumberOfStudents() can safely return int. Alternatively, change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update the UML and related methods to use long consistently.
